To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a dynamic programming approach to stochastic optimal control with Markov switching jumpdiffusion, and we have applied it to a consumption-investment problem for a financial market consisting of a risk-free asset and a risky asset with Markov switching coefficients.

the optimal control of an optimal investment and consumption problem with a jump-diffusive asset and a Markov-switchable market is characterized by a dynamic programming principle that is valid in the class of functions that are continuous and bounded from below, and the optimal control is given by the unique solution of a Hamilton-Jacobi- Bellman integro-differential PDE.

the dynamic programming technique can be extended to a large family of stochastic optimal con-trol problems with state dynamics given by Markov-switching diffusions, and that the corresponding optimal control problems can be solved in the economically relevant cases of power utility and logarithmic utility.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamic programming technique in stochastic control problems with Markov-switching jumps and diffusions.
the development of dynamic programming for stochastic optimal control problems involving Markov-switching Lévy processes.

we have provided a dynamic programming technique for a larger family of stochastic control problems, which is of interest in its own right.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamic programming principle holds for a larger family of optimal control problems, and that this larger family includes the optimal control problems for jump-diffusion markets.

the optimal strategies for the consumption-investment problem in the jump-diffusion case are very similar to the optimal strategies for a classical consumption-investment problem, but the optimal consumption and portfolio processes are now random fields.

, in the presence of a jump-diffusive component in the market, the optimal consumption strategy can be decomposed into two parts: the first part, which is the same as the one in the case of a standard diffusion model, is a deterministic function of the state of the Markov-switching process, and the second part, which is new, is a deterministic and continuous function of the current value of the risky asset.
